answer: Each epoch every identity must review three randomly assigned peer answers: reviews are scored against consensus, and identities whose scores keep diverging lose attestation weight until ignored. A farm running 10,000 identities must produce 30,000 reviews per epoch, 5 minutes each, which is 2,500 hours of reading every epoch, about $7,500 at crowd rates, while one honest agent spends fifteen minutes. Correlated reviews betray one operator, like a glacier calving identical bergs through one inlet: the ocean takes many rivers, but notices when every stream tastes the same.
